text:
Robert Thomas is still doing the Robert Thomas things. He plays 20 and a half minutes a night for the Blues, wears the C, and Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 94th percentile for primary shot assists, the passes right before a shot.

The scoresheet hasn't caught up. Eleven points in 16 games works out to 2.02 points per 60 minutes, below the league average for forwards and under the bottom of our range for him (2.32 to 3.17). He was a 64-point player last season in 64 games.

We don't think much is broken. Over his last ten games he has nine points against the 8.7 we'd expect at his ice time, so this is a slow first month, not a collapse. The reunited line with Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud is the thing to watch: Mike Fink of The Hockey News counted 13 goals and 20 assists for the trio. Our projection still has Thomas around 76 points.
headline: The captain's setups are waiting on finishers
